title: COP31: Fossil fuels still missing from draft deal at UN climate summit
summary: Countries are still deeply divided despite weeks of negotiations. Nations are now mulling over a new draft text that still doesn't mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming. DW has more.
byline: Emmy Sasipornkarn, Nik Martin, Dmytro Hubenko, Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Karl Sexton

image.caption: Activists protested the failure of COP31 after a second draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels Image: Umit Bektas/REUTERS

blocks.text: What we know about the latest COP31 draft deal
The third draft makes no mention of the words "fossil," "oil," "coal," or "phase out."
However, as in the second draft, the latest version retains a goal to boost electricity's share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, as well as efforts to expand the use of "clean energy."
The draft text also does not stipulate that the "35-by-35" electrification target should be met using renewable energy sources.
It also urges countries to "accelerate" carbon capture and storage — a controversial technology backed by the fossil fuel industry.
